items.title: Batteries the key to unlocking an energy revolution, and one state is racing ahead
items.description: Western Australia in particular is proving to the world that grid-scale batteries are no longer a complementary technology but can play a central role in power grids.

items.title: 'We need to talk about sex': Young people call for sex ed to grow up
items.description: A long-running survey of Australian teens has identified falling condom use and unwanted sex as major concerns for young people starting relationships.

items.title: May's wet weather rainfall defies expectations amid low pressure systems
items.description: A series of low-pressure systems are drenching Australia this week, quickly turning this May into one of the wettest on record for parts of the country's east.

items.title: Young saviour and an answered prayer deliver Blues incredible Origin win
items.description: When the Blues needed heroes to get on top of the Maroons in State of Origin I, they turned to a debutante and the oldest player on the field.

items.title: Labor's CGT challenge deepens as biotech sector raises alarm
items.description: Another sector has called for a capital gains tax change carve-out, warning the government that it will face a talent drain without it.

items.title: Live: Budget's negative gearing, CGT legislation to be introduced to parliament
items.description: The federal government will introduce legislation to parliament today to overhaul negative gearing and the capital gains tax. Follow live.

items.title: Israel warns all residents in southern Lebanon to leave
items.description: It is the first time Israel has made such a sweeping demand since US President Donald Trump announced in April a ceasefire had been imposed in Lebanon.

items.title: UK's social media ban could be harsher than Australia's. Here's how it compares
items.description: The UK could become the latest nation to implement a social media ban, after British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer vowed to introduce a "game changer" policy.

items.title: Man joins brother and late mother's reconciliation journey after discovering he is Indigenous
items.description: Iain Seymour didn't realise he was Aboriginal until he discovered he was adopted and learned that his mother played a key role in a memorial to the long-term effects of the Stolen Generations. Warning: This story contains images of Indigenous people who have died.

items.title: Divers begin complex mission to rescue men found alive in flooded Laos cave
items.description: Five of the seven people, who entered the cave in central Laos more than a week ago, have been found alive. Rescuers are still searching for two.

items.title: Matthew Perry's assistant jailed for role in Friends actor's death
items.description: Matthew Perry's live-in personal assistant, who had a central role in the Friends star's descent into ketamine addiction and injected him with the fatal dose of the drug, has been sentenced to three years and five months in prison.

items.title: Live: ABC experts take your questions about Iran war as it enters fourth month
items.description: ABC experts are taking questions abut the Iran war as the conflict enters its fourth month with no clear end in sight. Follow live.

items.title: Melbourne teacher goes missing in India
items.description: The family of maths teacher Sunil Sharma say the 66-year-old disappeared nearly a week ago, while trying to sell a property in the Punjabi city of Amritsar.

items.title: Legal action filed over federal government's land clearing decision
items.description: The federal environment minister's decision to wave through plans to bulldoze almost 3,000 hectares — an area 10 times the size of Sydney's CBD — of habitat, home to threatened species, will be challenged in the Federal Court.

items.title: Why this photo has been terrifying the internet for years
items.description: Forget about slashers and body horror — the next evolution of fright stems from an fluorescent-lit room.

items.title: Torquay wagtails increasing in numbers around the world
items.description: A Victorian artist paints hundreds of willie wagtails a week to give away locally and now they're popping up all over the world.

items.title: Quiz: Can you identify Aussie TV shows from a single frame?
items.description: How well do you know your Neighbours from your Deadloch? Take our single-frame Australian TV quiz to find out.

items.title: 'Like sugar to a human': Farmers look to move away from nitrogen 'hit'
items.description: A war thousands of kilometres away from Australia's farms is quietly reshaping what crops are planted and what will be available at supermarkets in the future.

items.title: Esperance on cusp of expanding biofuel industry
items.description: In the 1990s, Esperance was seen as a key to a major biofuels industry for Western Australia. Thirty years later, the industry has seen little change. But some say the area has untapped potential as a major fuel supplier.

items.title: Live: ASX set top open lower as price of oil drops
items.description: The Aussie share market is set to open lower as the price of oil drops. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Breaking: Man charged with murder after several people attacked in regional Queensland
items.description: A 36-year-old man has been charged with murder after allegedly attacking several people south of Bundaberg.

items.title: Police charge five teens after stolen car rampage in Cairns
items.description: After chaotic scenes in Cairns yesterday morning, police say they have arrested five teenagers.

items.title: Modelling suggests 'second wave' of algal bloom in Spencer Gulf
items.description: Modelling predicts that the algal bloom that has plagued South Australia's coastlines since March 2025 will be moving further through the Spencer Gulf in the next few months.

items.title: 'How low will they stoop?' Apology demanded over leak to media
items.description: A Tasmanian independent politician is calling for an apology after her personal health-related request via email to the government was leaked to a media outlet.

items.title: WA teachers to be trained to better support children with higher needs
items.description: The WA government has committed $16 million for a professional learning hub that will include mandatory inductions for special needs education assistants and disability modules for graduate teachers.
